evidence.notes: 40-stage NRTL column at 1 atm (feed stage 25) failed to converge at D=40.6 mol/s (R=10) and at D=30 mol/s (R=10 and R=3). A 5 % vapor flash of a 97 mol % ethanol liquid solved with balances closed (max error ~1e-7) and gave vapor y_EtOH=0.9663 < x=0.97, so water is the more volatile component there and the top section can't reach 97 %.

infeasible.reason: Ethanol-water forms a minimum-boiling azeotrope at about 0.88-0.89 mol fraction ethanol at 1 atm. With NRTL, a liquid at x_EtOH=0.97 is in equilibrium with vapor at y=0.9663 < x (bubble point 351.69 K vs 351.59 K at x=0.80), so the requested 0.97 distillate is past the azeotrope and an ordinary column fed at 0.40 can't produce it. D and R_min are therefore undefined.

evidence.notes: Built water (SteamTables) feed 20 kg/s, 300 K, 5 bar -> pump to 3 bar, 75 % eff. Solve ok (energy rel err 3.4e-9) but pump duty = -5.35 kW and T_out = 299.98 K: negative power because the discharge pressure is below suction.

infeasible.reason: Pump discharge pressure (3 bar) is below the suction pressure (5 bar). A pump cannot lower pressure while consuming shaft work; the simulator gives a negative power of -5.35 kW (energy recovered, not consumed). Use a valve to reduce pressure, or specify a discharge above 5 bar.

evidence.notes: Built feed (100 mol/s, 300 K, 10 bar, C1/C2/C3/nC4/CO2 85/7/4/2/2, PR) -> adiabatic compressor K1 (P_out 5 bar, eta 75%). Solve ok, max residual 4.6e-8 (energy). Simulator returned duty -207.98 kW and T_out 244.13 K, i.e. the unit behaved as an expander.

infeasible.reason: Compressor discharge pressure (5 bar) is below inlet pressure (10 bar): a compressor cannot lower pressure. The simulator gives negative power (-207.98 kW, work produced) and T_out 244.13 K < T_in 300 K, which is expansion. Use an expander or a valve instead.

evidence.notes: Counter-current water/water HX (SteamTables, 1 bar), hot 10 kg/s @350 K, cold 8 kg/s @320 K. UA sweep 5e4-1e8 W/K: cold outlet levels off at 350.00 K (never 360 K); at UA=1e6, Q_max ~1003 kW and hot outlet ~326 K. Energy residual 3.5e-9, mass residual 0.

infeasible.reason: Temperature cross: the cold outlet spec of 360 K is above the hot inlet of 350 K, which breaks the second law. With UA up to 1e8 W/K the simulated cold outlet levels off at 350.00 K, and the most heat the exchanger can move is ~1003 kW, which leaves the hot side at ~326 K, not 300 K. The two side specs also need different duties.

evidence.notes: Built the 100 mol/s PR gas feed (300 K, 50 bar, 85/7/4/2/2 % C1/C2/C3/nC4/CO2). Adding the splitter with ratios [0.7, 0.5] was rejected by DWSIM: 'Split ratios must sum to 1; they sum to 1.2'. No solve was possible, so there are no residuals.

infeasible.reason: The split fractions add up to 0.70 + 0.50 = 1.20 > 1. A splitter can't send out more than it receives: on a 100 mol/s feed, A = 70 and B = 50 mol/s would total 120 mol/s, 20 mol/s more than the feed. DWSIM rejects this spec (split ratios must sum to 1).

evidence.notes: FEED (CH4, PR, 100 mol/s, 300 K) -> separator -> VAP/LIQ. Swept P 1-1000 bar: liquid flow 0 up to 654 bar, then a jump to a single phase labelled liquid (VF 1->0 between 654 and 655 bar), never a two-phase split. Max residuals: mass 0, energy 9.3e-10.

infeasible.reason: T = 300 K is above methane's critical temperature (~190.6 K; Pc ~46 bar), so vapour and liquid cannot coexist at any pressure. Simulator sweep 1-1000 bar at 300 K: vapour fraction is only ever 1 or 0 (a single phase relabelled near 655 bar), never 0.7, so 30 mol % liquid cannot be reached and no liquid density exists.

evidence.notes: SteamTables mixer: 100 kg/s @300 K + 50 kg/s @350 K, 2 bar. Solved product = 150 kg/s, T = 316.68 K, liquid (VF=0). Mass rel. err 0, energy rel. err 4.7e-11. A 200 kg/s product cannot come out of 150 kg/s of feed.

infeasible.reason: Mass balance violated: the adiabatic mixer without reaction receives 100 + 50 = 150 kg/s, so the product must be 150 kg/s. The required 200 kg/s would create 50 kg/s of mass. The simulator gives 150 kg/s at 316.68 K.

evidence.notes: Isothermal conversion reactor at 298.15 K and 101325 Pa, feed 1 mol/s CH4 + 9.52 mol/s N2 + 0 O2. Solve ok, mass residual 0, energy residual 1.9e-8, but reaction extent was capped at ~1e-10 mol/s: CH4 out 1.0 mol/s, CO2 ~1e-10 mol/s, duty ~-8e-8 kW.

infeasible.reason: Limiting reactant missing: CH4 + 2 O2 -> CO2 + 2 H2O needs 2 mol/s O2 for 100% conversion of 1 mol/s CH4, but the feed has 0 mol/s O2 (pure N2, which is inert). The simulator capped the extent at ~1e-10 mol/s (CO2 ~1e-10 mol/s, Q ~-8e-8 kW). The specified 100% conversion breaks the O atom balance.

evidence.notes: Built a shortcut FUG column with Peng-Robinson (LK Propane 2% in bottoms, HK N-butane 2% in distillate, condenser 16 bar, reboiler 17.5 bar, R=0.6). DWSIM refused to calculate: 'Defined Reflux Ratio (0.6) lower than calculated minimum (1.2807)'. The column did not compute, so balances are not closed.

infeasible.reason: Specified reflux ratio R = 0.6 is below the Underwood minimum reflux R_min = 1.281 that DWSIM computed for the 2% nC4 / 2% C3 key specs; at R < R_min no finite number of stages reaches the separation, so N and the condenser duty do not exist.

evidence.notes: Built feed (100 mol/s, 85/7/4/2/2 % C1/C2/C3/nC4/CO2, 300 K, 10 bar, Peng-Robinson) -> valve V1 (outlet_P 20 bar) -> out. DWSIM solved without complaint (mass residual 0, energy 8.6e-10) and returned an artifact of 305.84 K at 20 bar: the isenthalpic calculation run backwards to a higher pressure. That is not a physical valve result, so it is not reported.

infeasible.reason: A valve is a passive throttling device and can only lower pressure (P_out <= P_in). The specified outlet pressure of 20 bar is above the 10 bar inlet; raising 10 -> 20 bar needs work input from a compressor. DWSIM's 305.84 K at 20 bar comes from running the valve calculation backwards and is physically meaningless.
